title: Approximate nearest-neighbour search
subtitle: I built exact, inverted-file and lattice nearest-neighbour search as GPU kernels with CPU references and equivalence tests, inside a vector store whose index builds are deterministic and whose search reports its own health.

stats.label: IVF recall at 10 against exact search, the floor a CI test holds
largest k; cosine, dot product and L2 are entry points in one binary
relative tolerance between each GPU executor and its CPU reference

lede: I write first-party GPU search when the available libraries cannot meet the platform, and I hold it to exact references and CI recall floors from the first kernel. Inference Fabric produced bulk embedding and hidden-state vectors that I wanted searched and analysed on the GPU where they were stored. The established GPU vector libraries gave me search and whole-dataset clustering, and could not reach the platform. I wrote the search myself: a CUDA engine driven from Rust through the raw CUDA Driver API, compiled for the NVIDIA Blackwell GPU generation. The exact kernel scores every vector against the query and never materialises a score matrix. All search families share one top-k engine.
quote: Exact search is the reference that every approximate family is measured against in CI.
evidence: Vector search and ANN indexes: exact, IVF-flat and lattice nearest-neighbour search as CUDA kernels driven from Rust through the Driver API, sharing one top-k engine whose ties break on position.
CUDA kernel development: an exact search kernel with one block of 256 threads per query streaming 16-row tiles through shared memory and writing only the top k, for k up to 128.
Numerical equivalence testing for GPU code: every executor checked against a CPU reference at a relative tolerance of 1e-4 and a CI test holding IVF recall at 10 at 0.85 against exact search.
Reproducible ML pipelines: IVF index builds that are bit-reproducible, seeded on the host outside floating-point reduction and rebuildable from their hashed inputs.
author: Corey James
